sections.sectionText: Honors section of FSHN 120: Contemporary Nutrition. Explore the impact of food on health and wellness with an emphasis on critical thinking, reflective learning, and experiential engagement. Students will examine nutrition concepts in depth, connect course material to real-world issues such as food insecurity and health disparities, and collaborate on applied projects designed to strengthen academic and professional skills. As an Honors section, the course emphasizes discussion, active learning, and leadership in both classroom and community contexts. ***If you’re a James Scholar or honors student who wants to complete an honors project in FSHN 120, you may enroll in the online section (CRN 57561). The instructor will provide additional opportunities to complete an approved honors project there. Questions? Email burkhalt@illinois.edu.

sections.sectionText: ****If interested, contact Chloe Morrell chloem@illinois.edu for an interview.*** Title: Performance Nutrition Experience with Illini Athletics and Illini Fuel.This 2-credit hour course provides students with an immersive, hands-on opportunity to work alongside Illini Athletics and the Illini Fuel program at the University of Illinois. Students will gain valuable experience in performance nutrition, contributing to the preparation, delivery, and management of athlete-focused nutritional support. Enrollment requires successfully passing an interview process followed by a background check conducted by the Department of Intercollegiate Athletics prior to the first week of class. Students will commit to ~6 hours per week (totaling 100 hours) over the semester, including early morning and late evening shifts. Attendance and participation are critical, with each 2-hour shift contributing 2% toward the final grade. Students must arrive on time with a positive "can-do" attitude and remain until formal dismissal to earn this credit. This course is ideal for students passionate about performance nutrition, seeking to develop practical skills and gain professional experience in a dynamic environment that directly supports athletic performance and recovery.

sections.sectionText: SURVEY OF YOUTH-RELATED APPLIED EXTENSION RESEARCH AND PROGRAMMING course overview: Youth programming is vital to University of Illinois Extension efforts. Learn about applied Extension research being conducted by Illinois Extension scholars and professionals focused on youth, ranging from STEM learning, technology, school food programs, nature, and inclusion of youth in program planning, among other topics. Students will explore the public engagement mission area of the university through exposure to youth-based content. Information regarding translation of research into educational programs for youth will be presented.

sections.sectionText: This will be a project-based course with a flexible schedule. You will work directly with the instructor to determine the schedule. The course involves learning advanced topics such as differential analysis in discrimination tests, Thurstonian modeling, multivariate techniques, clustering, and biometrics, with students managing a research project related to these areas. Weekly meetings with the instructor will guide progress, but students should expect to dedicate at least five additional hours per week to complete the assignments and learning goals. The flexible schedule allows students to work closely with the instructor. The final assessment will be a literature review or research paper based on their findings. This course emphasizes self-directed learning, critical thinking, and hands-on experience in sensory science research.

sections.sectionText: This course explores the gut microbiome and its influence on animals’ health, nutrition, and physiology. Students will learn about microbial diversity across niches, factors shaping gut communities, and the roles of microbiota in host function. Emphasis is placed on current methods for microbiome analysis, including bioinformatic tools and data interpretation. Through discussions and literature review, students will examine emerging research, opportunities, and challenges in studying microbial ecosystems in animals.

The application of fermentation to create food ingredients (amino acids, enzymes, nucleotides, etc.) will be discussed. Students who previously took FSHN 471 may not take this section of NUTR 510 for credit.

sections.sectionText: Title: Current and Emerging Topics in Food and Agricultural Engineering *** First two classes will meet Jan 9, 2026 and Jan 16, 2026, and will be recorded to watch at a later date if needed. *** This multi-institutional course provides a broad perspective of innovation as applied to food engineering. The course will provide a general overview and case studies of current and emerging research areas in food and agricultural engineering and processing by different research groups in the nation. The course will demonstrate the efforts among food engineers and scientists in the nation to advance engineering knowledge and technologies for the purpose of improving food safety, quality and security, and enhance health benefits of food products through extensive research in focused areas.
